newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt firmer in Europe, eyes on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt firmer in Europe, eyes on U.S. data.

text.p: LONDON, May 12 (Reuter) Brady bond prices were mostly firmer on Monday but market experts said trading activity was light and expected to remain that way ahead of key U.S. inflation reports later in the week.

"The market will not do much in front of (the U.S. inflation) numbers and will trade off the numbers as they come in. I think the market it will be rangebound until then," said an emerging market trader at a U.S. investment bank.
U.S. data expected this week include April retail sales on Tuesday, producer prices on Wednesday and consumer prices on Thursday.
Nervousness about continued dollar weakness against the yen will also be a focal point for the emerging debt markets this week, trading sources said.

"A week ago we were looking at 127 (on dollar/yen) but we are now looking at 118 and that hurts because most of our instruments are dollar-denominated," said Richard Gray, emerging market analyst at BankAmerica in London.

"Suddenly, anybody taking a currency perspective on our asset allocation has to rethink whether the dollar is going down or whether a retreat like this is a buying opportunity for dollar instruments," Gray added.
Concerns the Bank of Japan (BOJ) may raise its official discount rate, currently 0.50 percent, may also pressure the prices of dollar-denominated assets over the longer term, market sources said.

"It's the old trickle down effect. If you see it (a discount rate hike by the BOJ) affect the G7 assets you will definitely see it affect the emerging market assets," said a trader at a European bank in London.
Bulgarian Brady instruments firmed following news the country's consumer prices fell 0.7 percent in April after rising 12.3 percent in March.

Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were 1/2 stronger at 65-1/4 bid and its FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were 3/8 higher at 49-5/8 bid. Poland's Brady bonds also gained on hopes the country would receive a credit rating upgrade from rating agencies this year.
Poland's par bonds PO275024=RR were 5/8 firmer at 56 bid and the country's PDI bonds PO325024=RR were 1/8 better at 83-3/4 bid.
"IBCA is supposed to be in Poland this week and S&P made a positive comment on Friday so we are fairly positive that it will get a credit ratings hike," the first trader said.
On Friday, Standard and Poor's said Poland's credit trend was fairly positive and it would be monitoring the upcoming parliamentarty elections.
Elsewhere, Argentine FRBS ARFLC05 were 1/8 higher at 92-3/8 and Venezuelan DCBs VZFLL07RR were 1/8 firmer at 89-3/8 bid.
